subject: Clarify Service Provider vs Processor: CCPA/CPRA addendum for Acme Health
messages:
From: Jordan Fields <jordan.fields@acmehealth.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Acme Health Legal <privacy@acmehealth.com>
Date: Fri, 21 May 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: CCPA/CPRA — are you a 'service provider' or 'processor'?

Hi Soojin,

Quick question as we're wrapping the vendor review: under CCPA/CPRA Acme treats vendors as either 'service providers' (no sale) or 'processors' under the EU rules. For our procurement/legal team we need to confirm: will Redwood be legally designated a Service Provider under CCPA/CPRA in the addendum? Specifically we're looking for language that: (1) prohibits "sale"/commercialization of Acme personal data, (2) limits onward transfers to subcontractors only under written agreements enforcing the same restrictions, and (3) clarifies retention and deletion obligations for user data.

Also, we have a short list of subprocessors we expect to see named or a process for notifications — is that something you can provide quickly? Our privacy counsel (Megan Ross) is cc'd. We're hoping to finalize this week.

Thanks,
Jordan
Jordan Fields
Senior Product Manager, Integrations
Acme Health

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jordan Fields <jordan.fields@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 21 May 2026 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: CCPA/CPRA — are you a 'service provider' or 'processor'?

Hi Jordan — thanks for the clear ask. Short answer: yes, our standard position is to be designated as a Service Provider under CCPA/CPRA. We do not "sell" personal data and we restrict onward transfers to subprocessors under written agreements that impose the same limitations.

I've looped in Karthik (privacy/legal) and Laura (sales ops) to confirm exact wording and provide our subprocessor process. We'll draft an addendum that includes:
- explicit "Service Provider" designation under CPRA/CCPA;
- prohibition on sale;
- retention/deletion triggers tied to contract termination and documented retention schedule;
- subprocessors clause with notification and objection window.

Can you share Acme's preferred timeline and any redline language your counsel needs? We'll upload a draft addendum and track via the HubSpot deal.

Best,
Soojin
Soojin Lee
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 25 May 2026 08:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: CCPA/CPRA — are you a 'service provider' or 'processor'?

Soojin/Laura — drafting notes below for the addendum. Copy paste-ready language in brackets.

1) Designation: We should accept "Service Provider" under the CPRA/CCPA section. Proposed: "For the purposes of the California Consumer Privacy Act (CCPA)/California Privacy Rights Act (CPRA), Redwood Inference shall be deemed a 'Service Provider' (as defined in the CCPA/CPRA) in relation to Customer Personal Information processed on Customer's behalf."

2) No sale: Add explicit non-sale clause. Proposed: "Redwood does not sell, nor will it retain, use, or disclose Customer Personal Information for commercial purposes unrelated to providing the contracted services."

3) Subprocessors: We have a maintained subprocessors list; we will provide to Acme and agree to notify 30 days prior to adding new subprocessors. Proposed: "Redwood may engage subprocessors subject to written agreements that impose data processing obligations at least as protective as this Addendum. Redwood will notify Customer in advance of any new subprocessors and will allow Customer a 14-day review/objection period."

4) Data transfers & retention: Ensure we include deletion/return language on termination and documented retention schedule for logs/telemetry. Proposed: "Upon termination, Redwood will, at Customer's election, delete or return Customer Personal Information, except to the extent retention is required by law; for telemetry/operational logs Redwood will retain aggregated or pseudonymized records only and will purge raw logs per the retention schedule."

Notes: Megan (Acme counsel) may request a shorter objection period or additional audit rights; flag to Soojin if they push for vendor-hosted audits. Also recommend attaching our redlined addendum and the current subprocessors roster.

-Karthik
Principal Counsel, Privacy & Security
Redwood Inference

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jordan Fields <jordan.fields@acmehealth.com>, Acme Health Legal <privacy@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 27 May 2026 11:17:00 -07:00
Subject: Draft CCPA/CPRA Service Provider addendum (redwood_ccpa-addendum_v2)

Hi Jordan / Megan — attached is a draft addendum that incorporates the points we discussed. High-level:
- Redwood accepts Service Provider status under CCPA/CPRA and excludes sale of data;
- We provide a subprocessors roster and will notify 30 days in advance of changes;
- We allow a 14-day review window for new subprocessors and provide operational retention details in Section 3;
- Deletion/return options on termination with limited exceptions for legal hold.

Attachments: redwood_ccpa-addendum_v2.pdf (proposed), acme_requested_clarifications_20260525.docx (our response matrix). Also shared a Google Drive link for collaborative redlines.

Next steps: please review and send any redlines — if Acme prefers DocuSign we can route it that way. If Megan wants to discuss any audit or subcontractor questions, we can set a call with Karthik this week.

Thanks,
Soojin
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference

From: Jordan Fields <jordan.fields@acmehealth.com>

Cc: Acme Health Legal <privacy@acmehealth.com>, Megan Ross <megan.ross@rosslaw.com>
Date: Thu, 28 May 2026 16:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Draft CCPA/CPRA Service Provider addendum (redwood_ccpa-addendum_v2)

Soojin — got it, thanks. Quick clarifying Q: in your proposed subprocessors clause you reference a 14-day review/objection window but Karthik's note also mentions a 30-day notification for additions — can you confirm the sequence (i.e., we get notified 30 days before a new subprocessor goes live, then we have 14 days to object)? Megan — cc'd — will likely propose 21 days total but wants to confirm retention language first. We'll get redlines back by Tuesday if all good.

Appreciate the fast turnaround.
Jordan
